stories.title: Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026, the Winning Images
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: The winners of this year's Wildlife Photographer of the Year competition have just been revealed, chosen from a record-breaking number of entries from around the globe. The winning images capture incredible, rarely-seen moments from nature, from close encounters with wild animals to breathtaking landscapes. Photographers from many different countries were honored, celebrating the beauty and diversity of life on Earth. These photos remind us why protecting wild places matters so much. It's a joyful showcase of talent and the natural world working together.
stories.why_good: A completed, concrete event celebrating nature and human creativity, with no suffering or controversy at its core.

stories.title: Pittsburgh Water Launches Debt Forgiveness Program to Help Families with Rising Costs
stories.label: government
stories.summary: Pittsburgh's water authority just rolled out a new program that wipes away old water bill debt for struggling residents over a 24-month period. Customers who qualify have already been enrolled as of September, and all they need to do is keep up with their regular monthly payments going forward. This takes a real weight off families who've been falling behind as utility costs climb. It's a practical, already-working fix, not just a promise on paper.
stories.why_good: A local government agency took concrete action to relieve real financial burden on families, and the program is already enrolling people, not just proposed.

stories.title: Teen Triathlete Raises More Than $30,000 to Donate Bikes and Riding Lessons to Low-Income Families
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A Georgia teen named Jonathan Thai turned his love of triathlons into a mission to help others. His nonprofit, the Pedal Forward Foundation, has now raised over $30,000 to give bicycles and free riding lessons to kids and families who couldn't otherwise afford them. Hundreds of children have already received bikes and learned to ride safely. It's a sweet reminder of how one young person's passion can turn into real help for a whole community.
stories.why_good: A real, completed charitable effort that has already put bikes in the hands of hundreds of low-income kids and taught them to ride — concrete help, not a plan.
